title: Signature Autonomous Ecosystem Builder Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Specifications, data sources, code generators, tests, and deployment records for creating connected database-and-tool ecosystems. The Signature Autonomous Ecosystem Builder Database is the capstone: how to build entire connected ecosystems — databases with their AIs, tools with their tests, generators with their guardrails — that build themselves further. Each record is a complete ecosystem specification: the databases it contains, the data sources feeding them, the code generators producing tools, the tests verifying everything, and the deployment records. This is the database that builds database networks — the machinery behind the march to a million, documented as a reproducible system.

title: Signature Autonomous Ecosystem Builder Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Ecosystem anatomy: SPECIFICATIONS (what to build, in what order, to what standard) -> SOURCES (data feeds with licenses and cadences) -> GENERATORS (code/data generators with hard caps, dedupe, self-regulation, output labeling) -> TESTS (per-database verification + cross-database: link integrity, dedupe across DBs, consistency) -> DEPLOYMENT (staged: build, verify, publish; rollback plans). Build order: foundations first (data infra), then disciplines, then applications. Quality gates per stage: spec review, cross-check (no duplicates), build verification, integration check. Generator guardrails: hard cap (10^15), throttle, duplicate detection, correctness verification, generated-vs-built labeling (never mixed). Growth discipline: sideways (new databases), never by thinning records; genuinely-complete topics marked complete with reason. Governance: data lock-in (added records immutable), provenance everywhere, audit trails.

demo.title: Execution: Bayesian knowledge tracing update
demo.code: let pL=0.3;const pT=0.2,pS=0.1,pG=0.25;function update(correct){const pC=pL*(1-pS)+(1-pL)*pG;const pLgiven=correct?(pL*(1-pS)/pC):(pL*pS/(pL*pS+(1-pL)*(1-pG)));pL=pLgiven+(1-pLgiven)*pT;return pL;}const responses=[1,1,0,1,1];const traj=responses.map(update);const mastered=traj[traj.length-1]>=0.95;J({final:+traj[traj.length-1].toFixed(3),mastered});assert(traj.every(v=>v>=0&&v<=1),'bkt-range');assert(traj[traj.length-1]>0.3,'bkt-learn');

demo.title: Verification: concept graph is a DAG
demo.code: const edges=[['arith','algebra'],['algebra','deriv'],['deriv','backprop']];const nodes=[...new Set(edges.flat())];function topo(){const indeg={};nodes.forEach(n=>indeg[n]=0);edges.forEach(([a,b])=>indeg[b]++);const q=nodes.filter(n=>indeg[n]===0);const order=[];while(q.length){const n=q.shift();order.push(n);edges.filter(e=>e[0]===n).forEach(([a,b])=>{if(--indeg[b]===0)q.push(b);});}return order;}const order=topo();J({order,isDAG:order.length===nodes.length});assert(order.length===nodes.length&&order.indexOf('arith')<order.indexOf('backprop'),'dag');
